Hotel Chinzanso

ホテル椿山荘東京

From your hotel: 48 min (Yamanote to Mejiro, then bus 白61), ¥420

The garden estate a Meiji-era prime minister, Yamagata Aritomo, bought in 1878, now a grand hotel. The pagoda is a nearly 700-year-old building moved here from Hiroshima. Fog rolls through the garden at 40 past every hour, 9 AM to 9 PM.

A 2020 guide says the garden is free for hotel guests and anyone using its restaurants, cafés or lobby lounge (Le Jardin), so a drink there covers you if anyone asks.

Ginza 4-chome

銀座四丁目, 和光

36 min from Chinzanso: walk to Edogawabashi, Yurakucho Line one train, ¥180

The answer Reddit gives for high-end Tokyo, far more often than anywhere else: flagship stores up and down Chuo-dori, with the Wako clock tower on the main crossing.

Leave Chinzanso after the 3:40 fog. Maison Hermès is 3 min away.

≈ 5:35 PM

Aman Tokyo

アマン東京, 33F

8 min on foot from Tokyo Station

The lobby is on the 33rd floor of Otemachi Tower. One Mile at a Time (2019): "the most insanely gorgeous lobby I've seen in my life," with 30 meter ceilings. The Lounge by Aman looks out over the Imperial Palace Gardens.

Same review: the hotel is open to the public. A drink at the lounge is the way to sit down; no booking was checked.

What people say

Reddit (90 threads, about 5,000 comments, 2018 to 2026): Ginza is the place named for high-end Tokyo, far ahead of anywhere else (“High end shopping, Ginza.”). Hotel lobbies barely come up there.

Hotel reviewers rave about the Aman lobby, and World’s 50 Best describes the Lounge by Aman’s “impressive views of the Imperial Palace Gardens.”

Closed today: Akasaka Palace, the State Guest House. Its official calendar shows it shut Oct 26 to 31.

If you want a bar after: Bvlgari Bar (Tokyo Midtown Yaesu, 45F, on Tokyo Station’s Yaesu side) or Mandarin Bar (Mandarin Oriental, Nihonbashi, 37F).
